---
title: "Volume 0: The Mathematical Primer"
description: "A foundational guide to kinematics, configuration space, Lie groups, spatial vector algebra, and analytical dynamics for The Geometry of Motion."
---

Before analyzing the geometry of moving physical bodies or designing nonlinear controllers, we must establish a rigorous, common mathematical language. Physical motion takes place in continuous three-dimensional space, but its computational representation and control analysis unfold across configuration manifolds, tangent bundles, and Lie groups.

**Volume 0: The Mathematical Primer** establishes these foundations systematically. It bridges classical matrix linear algebra with modern geometric mechanics, introducing mathematical tools used throughout the multi-volume *Geometry of Motion* series. Rather than duplicating all twelve chapters onto a single unwieldy webpage, this volume is structured as a modular, linked reading path where each chapter maintains its own focused review surface and canonical URL.

## Foundations of Kinematics and Geometry

The first six chapters develop the geometric language of spatial kinematics, transitioning from flat linear spaces to curved manifold representations:

1. [A Primer on Linear Algebra](vol0_ch01_linear_algebra.html) — Vector spaces, inner products, spectral decompositions, and projection operators.
2. [The Transition to State Space](vol0_ch02_state_space.html) — First-order differential systems, phase portraits, and coordinate representations.
3. [Configuration Space and Degrees of Freedom](vol0_ch03_configuration.html) — Topology of generalized coordinates, holonomic constraints, and manifold structure.
4. [Rotations, Quaternions, and SO(3)](vol0_ch04_rotations_se3.html) — Lie group $\mathrm{SO}(3)$, unit quaternions, Euler angle singularities, and geodesic metrics.
5. [Twists, Wrenches, and the Screw Axis](vol0_ch05_screw_axes.html) — Chasles' theorem, screw coordinates, dual vectors, and reciprocal screw systems.
6. [Exponential Coordinates and Matrix Logarithms](vol0_ch06_exponential_coordinates.html) — Mapping between the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{se}(3)$ and the Lie group $\mathrm{SE}(3)$.

## Dynamics and Computational Algorithms

The remaining six chapters develop recursive kinematics, computational multibody mechanics, and analytical formulations:

7. [Recursive Algorithms](vol0_ch07_recursive_algorithms.html) — Kinematic trees, forward kinematics, and topological sorting of kinematic graphs.
8. [Spatial Vector Algebra and Inertia](vol0_ch08_spatial_algebra.html) — Featherstone spatial vectors, spatial inertia tensors, and coordinate transformation laws.
9. [The Product of Exponentials Formula](vol0_ch09_product_of_exponentials.html) — Brockett's POE formula for open kinematic chains in space and body frames.
10. [The Articulated Body Algorithm](vol0_ch10_articulated_body_algorithm.html) — $O(n)$ forward dynamics via articulated body inertias and pass-based recursions.
11. [Lagrangian Mechanics](vol0_ch11_lagrangian_mechanics.html) — Variational principles, Euler-Lagrange equations, and kinetic-potential energy partitions.
12. [Machine Learning and Neural Networks](vol0_ch12_machine_learning.html) — Function approximation, physics-informed representations, and gradient-based parameter estimation.

## Prerequisites and Next Steps

Readers should be familiar with multivariable calculus and introductory ordinary differential equations. After mastering the mathematical primer, proceed directly to [Volume I](volume1.html) for tangent-space methods, exact first-variation equations, their finite-perturbation limits, and contraction theory.
